summary: Angoon Seaplane Base (AGN/PAGN) is a small public-use seaplane base located in Angoon, a remote Tlingit community on Admiralty Island in southeastern Alaska. The facility primarily serves local residents, fishermen, and visitors accessing the surrounding Tongass National Forest wilderness area. Operating without a conventional runway, it functions as a vital lifeline for transportation in this isolated island community where road access is nonexistent.
faqs:
Q: What type of aircraft use Angoon Seaplane Base?
A: The base exclusively accommodates float-equipped seaplanes, as there is no conventional runway. Most flights are operated by small single-engine bush planes carrying up to 9 passengers.

Q: When is the base operational?
A: Operations are typically limited to daylight hours and favorable weather conditions. Winter operations can be limited due to ice and reduced daylight, while summer is the busiest season.

Q: Are there facilities at the terminal?
A: Facilities are minimal, typical of remote Alaskan seaplane bases, with a small dock area for loading and unloading passengers. No major amenities are available on-site.

Q: Can I fly here from Juneau?
A: Yes, short charter and scheduled flights connect Angoon to Juneau, approximately 60 miles northwest, with flight times under 30 minutes.
transport_tips: Ground transportation in Angoon is limited; plan to have accommodations arrange pickup from the seaplane dock or arrange a rental vehicle in advance. Ferry service from Juneau is an alternative but takes significantly longer than flying. Pack light, as baggage space on small seaplanes is restricted.
local_tip: Bring a light waterproof jacket even in summer; weather on Admiralty Island can shift rapidly, and small craft advisories are common when departing the base.
